sections.summary: The neutral reading identifies the woman as Israel/the covenant community, clothed in cosmic imagery and laboring to give birth to the messianic child; the section establishes symbolic identity rather than addressing the believer's standing before God.
The neutral reading describes the dragon's appearance, power, and attempt to devour the child at birth, establishing the cosmic antagonist without addressing the believer's standing before God.

sections.section_title: The Male Child and the Woman's Flight
sections.summary: The neutral reading narrates the male child's enthronement at God's throne and the woman's divinely prepared refuge in the wilderness for 1,260 days, describing God's protective action in cosmic narrative rather than addressing the believer's standing.

The neutral reading describes Michael's war with the dragon and the dragon's permanent expulsion from heaven, identified as the ancient serpent who deceives the whole world; the section narrates a cosmic event rather than addressing the believer's standing before God.

The neutral reading identifies a three-component victory formula by which the brothers overcame the accuser: the blood of the Lamb, the word of their testimony, and their willingness to die rather than recant.
sections.relevance: The three components of victory include both divine provision (the blood of the Lamb) and sustained human response (active testimony and willingness to die). The neutral reading notes that the verb 'overcame' (enikēsan) is the same verb used in all seven overcomer promises in the letters (2:7, 11, 17, 26; 3:5, 12, 21), where eschatological rewards are conditional on overcoming. The brothers' victory requires ongoing, active faithfulness -- not merely initial divine provision -- implying that the believer's standing involves continued participation in the Lamb's pattern of sacrificial faithfulness.
key_phrases: they overcame him because of the blood of the Lamb and because of the word of their testimony
they did not love their life even when faced with death

sections.section_title: The Dragon Pursues the Woman and Her Offspring
sections.summary: The neutral reading narrates the dragon's failed pursuit of the woman and his redirection of fury toward the rest of her offspring, defined as those who keep the commandments of God and hold to the testimony of Jesus.
sections.relevance: The faithful are identified by two present participles indicating ongoing action: 'those who keep (tērountōn) the commandments of God and hold (echontōn) the testimony of Jesus.' The neutral reading notes that these same two characteristics reappear verbatim in 14:12 to define the persevering saints. The identification of God's people by continuous obedience and sustained confession implies that belonging to the covenant community is characterized by ongoing fidelity, not a one-time status.
key_phrases: who keep the commandments of God and hold to the testimony of Jesus
